title: Forecast-to-Invoice Reconciliation: Workflow and Controls
author: Maya Shah
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines the operational workflow, controls, and escalation paths for reconciling committed forecasts (contracts, pipeline commitments, reserved capacity) to issued invoices and recognized revenue. It applies to monthly and quarterly close activities and to ongoing procurement-billing alignment for Dedicated and Private deployments. The objective is to ensure accuracy of billing, timely dispute resolution, and that revenue recognition inputs to RevRec are traceable to signed commercial terms.

Scope:
- Applies to all customer contracts that generate recurring or usage-based revenue (Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, Private deployments, professional services).
- Bridges three teams: Revenue Operations (Revenue Ops), Billing & AR, and Procurement/Contracting (Sales Ops & Legal as needed).

Key definitions:
- Forecast Commitment: Contractual or sales-committed quantity/value used in forecasts (e.g., committed monthly reserved capacity $/GPU/hr).
- Billing Event: Trigger that generates invoiceable usage (monthly metered, committed overage, one-time setup).
- Invoice-to-Forecast Delta: (Invoiced Amount - Forecasted Amount) / Forecasted Amount.
- Material Variance Threshold: Any Invoice-to-Forecast Delta > 5% or $5,000 (whichever is lower) is material and requires root-cause and remediation.

Owners and Roles:
- Finance (Billing & AR): Issue invoices, route disputes, maintain AR ledger. Primary owner for reconciliations and month-end invoice postings.
- Revenue Ops: Map contract terms to billing product SKUs, maintain forecast model and committed MRR/ARR.
- Procurement & Legal: Review and approve contract amendments that change billing triggers.
- Finance Systems (FP&A/Platform): Maintain GL codes, post adjusting entries, and update forecast rollups.

Cadence and Workflow (high level):
1) Daily: Near-real-time reconciliation dashboard updated from billing system (Stripe/Zuora/GCP Marketplace). Exceptions flagged for >10% daily movement.
2) Weekly: Revenue Ops and Billing run a delta report by customer, product, and contract. Variances >5% are triaged.
3) Monthly close window (Day -5 to Day +7): Formal forecast-to-invoice reconciliation, ownership sign-off, and posting of any adjusting journal entries before cutoff.
4) Quarterly: Deep-dive of recurring variance patterns and contract amendment sampling.

Detailed procedure: Monthly reconciliation (step-by-step)
1. Export datasets (Day -5):
   - Billing system: invoices, credit memos, unapplied payments for the prior month (CSV).
   - Revenue Ops: forecast committed amounts by customer and SKU (CSV).
   - Contracting: signed SOWs/amendments for the period (PDF links).

2. Normalize and join (Day -4):
   - Normalize SKUs and GL mapping using the canonical product mapping table (ProductCode -> GL Account).
   - Join on (CustomerID, ContractID, BillingPeriod).
   - Compute Invoice-to-Forecast Delta and create exception list.

3. Triage exceptions (Day -3 to Day -2):
   - Auto-resolve rules (no human action required): small rounding differences (< $50), unapplied payments that clear within AR workflow, known timing differences (trial-to-paid transition).
   - Manual review triggers: Material variance threshold breach, credit memos > 10% of invoice, unexpected SKUs billed. Assign to owner.

4. Root-cause and corrective actions (Day -2 to Day 0):
   - Common root causes: mis-mapped SKU, late contract amendment, usage meter misconfiguration, duplicate invoice.
   - Corrective actions: issue credit memo, reissue corrected invoice, adjust forecast and note in contract metadata, or post adjusting journal entry.
   - All corrective actions must include an audit comment referencing the ContractID and TicketID.

5. Sign-off and posting (Day 0 to Day +2):
   - Billing & AR owner posts final invoices/credit memos. FP&A posts adjusting journal entries with reference in the supporting schedule.
   - Revenue Ops approves the reconciliation schedule by customer and marks closed.

Escalation matrix: 
- Day 0 unresolved -> Escalate to Revenue Ops lead.
- Day 3 unresolved and material -> Escalate to Head of Finance and Legal (if contractual).
- Disputes involving > $50k or contractual interpretation -> Legal & Sales leadership review; temporary hold on revenue recognition pending resolution.

Controls and thresholds:
- Material variance threshold: >5% or $5,000.
- Invoice posting SLA: all corrected invoices/credit memos must be issued within 5 business days of identification.
- RevRec hold threshold: disputes > $50,000 or >20% of expected recognized revenue for the customer in the period.
- Audit trail: Every reconciliation row must have references for ContractID, InvoiceID, AR Ticket ID, and owner initials.

Integration points and datasets:
- Billing platform (Zuora/Stripe): Invoices, credit memos, payment records; export via API /billing/v1/invoices?period=YYYY-MM.
- Forecast model (internal db): committed_mrr table (CustomerID, ContractID, SKU, CommittedAmount, EffectiveDate).
- Contract repository (DocStore): canonical PDF link and amendment history.
- GL posting system (NetSuite/QuickBooks): Journal entry API endpoints for adjustments.

Example exception report (CSV columns):
CustomerID,ContractID,BillingPeriod,ForecastedAmount,InvoicedAmount,DeltaPct,RootCause,Owner,Status,Notes
ACME-001,CTR-2025-447,2026-06,12000,13800,15.0,Overage/UsageMeter,RevenueOps,in_review,"Investigating meter config; preliminary credit memo planned"

Templates and examples:
- Journal entry example (JSON payload to GL API):
{
  "date": "2026-06-30",
  "lines": [
    {"account": "Revenue-Deferred-400", "debit": "1800"},
    {"account": "Revenue-Recognized-401", "credit": "1800"}
  ],
  "memo": "Adjusting entry: reconcile forecast vs invoice for CTR-2025-447"
}

- Contract billing mapping table (sample):
| Contract Clause | Billing Trigger | SKU | GL Account | Notes |
|-----------------|-----------------|-----|------------|-------|
| Monthly reserved capacity | Monthly committed charge | RDW-DED-RES | 40110 | Applies when customer pins capacity |
| On-demand API tokens | Metered usage per 1k tokens | RDW-HOST-TOK | 40120 | Metered usage reported daily |

Exception handling examples:
- Duplicate invoice discovered: immediate cancellation note, reissue corrected invoice; log incident in Billing Queue with TicketID and tag 'duplicate-invoice'.
- Contract amendment effective mid-month: pro-rate invoice and tag both affected periods; update forecast and create audit entry linking to signed amendment PDF.

RevRec linkage and audit requirements:
- Every recognized revenue amount used for GAAP RevRec must be traceable to (a) a signed contract or amendment, (b) the posted invoice or approved credit memo, and (c) the reconciliation supporting schedule.
- The monthly reconciliation workbook is the single source of truth for differences and must be archived for 7 years.

Automation and tooling recommendations:
- Implement continuous reconciliation using a nightly ETL job that writes exception rows to a triage queue (e.g., Jira project: FNY-BILL).
- Add validation rules to the Revenue Ops product mapping service to reject unmapped SKUs at contract onboarding.
- Build a simple UI for Billing owners to apply common corrections (issue credit, re-bill) that records approval metadata.

Checklist before close (Day -1):
- [ ] Export billing and forecast datasets
- [ ] Run normalization script and generate exception CSV
- [ ] Triage and assign all exceptions > material threshold
- [ ] Confirm all planned corrective actions have tickets and owners
- [ ] Final sign-off from Billing & Revenue Ops leads

Audit & evidence retention:
- Reconciliation workbook (PDF), invoice PDFs, credit memos, contract PDFs, and Journal Entry IDs must be uploaded to the DocStore with naming convention: "recon/{YYYY-MM}/{CustomerID}/{ContractID}".
- Retention: 7 years for GAAP/audit purposes; 2 years for operational artifacts for internal reference.
